why: long_prereg_budget_addendum_2026-11-18.md: the registered week-swap null was too narrow (it averages out the models' real year-to-year differences) and the registered single-pitfall rule compared levels, not gains.
design: budget2_run.py with budget_lib.py unchanged: whole test years (2014-2025) swapped between the quantum model and its reference with probability 1/2, flips shared across grids; B = 1000 (seeds 43000+b); protocols: control, SEED, WINDOW, GRID, LOSS, QMODEL (each alone, REF control), ALL5. Statistic: gain = log ratio(control) - log ratio(protocol), in the same replicate.
decision_rule: Per protocol: 'beyond chance' if the observed gain exceeds the null 95th percentile of the gain, else 'within chance'. The share of null gains >= observed is reported as a one-sided p-value.
known_limits: Only 12 test years, so 4096 possible flips; 1000 random draws.
The null assumes yearly log ratios are symmetric around zero under no true difference.
Designed after seeing the week-swap result.
